# Findings on the Governing Medical‑Necessity Criteria for CPT 29827 (Rotator Cuff Repair) – BCBS Louisiana

## Summary of what I could verify

Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana (BCBSLA) does **not** review outpatient shoulder/rotator-cuff surgery under its own in-house medical policy library for most commercial members. BCBSLA's own Provider Office Manual (Section 4: Medical Management) and Provider Tidbit "TB00042010 – Inpatient/Outpatient Authorization Guide" state that prior authorization for **musculoskeletal (MSK) joint surgery — which includes shoulder arthroscopy/rotator cuff repair — is handled through the Carelon MBM Provider Portal**, i.e., delegated to **Carelon Medical Benefits Management** (formerly AIM Specialty Health), an independent utilization-management company under contract to BCBSLA. This applies to fully-insured, Small Business Funded (SBF), and OGB commercial members (not FEP). Reese's plan is described as commercial/ACA, so this program almost certainly governed the review of the CPT 29827 request.

The clinical criteria Carelon applies are published in its **Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines – Musculoskeletal, "Joint Surgery"** guideline, which has a dedicated "Shoulder Arthroscopy and Open Procedures" section covering rotator cuff repair. I was able to confirm this document is current, publicly posted, and load successfully (HTTP 200) at the URL below, and I retrieved partial verbatim language from it (and from its predecessor 2024 version, which has an identical structure) via direct fetch and search-indexed excerpts. However, the live page and its companion PDF are extremely long (70+ pages covering shoulder, hip, knee, meniscus, and cartilage surgery), and my fetch tool truncates extraction before reaching the full numbered rotator-cuff-repair criteria list — so I can give you accurately-sourced excerpts, but not a complete verbatim reproduction of every sub-bullet. I flag this limitation below.

I could **not** confirm that a separate BCBSLA-authored "medical policy" (as opposed to the delegated Carelon guideline) was the actual document applied to this specific denial — BCBSLA's own medical-policy search tool is a JavaScript application I could not query directly, and a candidate "Shoulder Surgeries" policy (No. SUR228) I found elsewhere could not be confirmed as belonging to BCBSLA (no branding evidence tied it to Louisiana Blue), so I am not presenting it as the governing document.

# Findings on the Governing Medical‑Necessity Criteria for CPT 29827 (Rotator Cuff Repair) – BCBS Louisiana

## Summary of what I could verify

Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana (BCBSLA) does **not** review outpatient shoulder/rotator-cuff surgery under its own in-house medical policy library for most commercial members. BCBSLA's own Provider Office Manual (Section 4: Medical Management) and Provider Tidbit "TB00042010 – Inpatient/Outpatient Authorization Guide" state that prior authorization for **musculoskeletal (MSK) joint surgery — which includes shoulder arthroscopy/rotator cuff repair — is handled through the Carelon MBM Provider Portal**, i.e., delegated to **Carelon Medical Benefits Management** (formerly AIM Specialty Health), an independent utilization-management company under contract to BCBSLA. This applies to fully-insured, Small Business Funded (SBF), and OGB commercial members (not FEP). Reese's plan is described as commercial/ACA, so this program almost certainly governed the review of the CPT 29827 request.

The clinical criteria Carelon applies are published in its **Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines – Musculoskeletal, "Joint Surgery"** guideline, which has a dedicated "Shoulder Arthroscopy and Open Procedures" section covering rotator cuff repair. I was able to confirm this document is current, publicly posted, and load successfully (HTTP 200) at the URL below, and I retrieved partial verbatim language from it (and from its predecessor 2024 version, which has an identical structure) via direct fetch and search-indexed excerpts. However, the live page and its companion PDF are extremely long (70+ pages covering shoulder, hip, knee, meniscus, and cartilage surgery), and my fetch tool truncates extraction before reaching the full numbered rotator-cuff-repair criteria list — so I can give you accurately-sourced excerpts, but not a complete verbatim reproduction of every sub-bullet. I flag this limitation below.

I could **not** confirm that a separate BCBSLA-authored "medical policy" (as opposed to the delegated Carelon guideline) was the actual document applied to this specific denial — BCBSLA's own medical-policy search tool is a JavaScript application I could not query directly, and a candidate "Shoulder Surgeries" policy (No. SUR228) I found elsewhere could not be confirmed as belonging to BCBSLA (no branding evidence tied it to Louisiana Blue), so I am not presenting it as the governing document.

**Bottom line for the appeal:** Regardless of which exact document controls, the stated denial reason ("no adequate trial of conservative treatment") tracks a standard requirement in both BCBSLA's delegated Carelon "Joint Surgery" guideline (6–12 weeks of physical therapy/home exercise plus NSAID trial and/or corticosteroid injection, unless contraindicated) and typical payer shoulder-surgery criteria generally. The strongest appeal will directly document: (1) total duration of conservative care attempted (PT visits/dates, home exercise program), (2) medication trials (NSAIDs) and/or corticosteroid injection dates and outcomes, (3) any contraindication if a component (e.g., injection) was skipped, and (4) physical exam findings and imaging (MRI) supporting a rotator cuff tear correlating with symptoms — and it should explicitly request that BCBSLA identify, in its written appeal response, the specific policy/guideline number and version applied to the original denial.
